title: What John Rance Had to Tell
question: Today, can Holmes get the murderer's own description out of a man who does not know he has it?

cab.described: The inside of a four-wheeled growler on a March afternoon in 1881, two men side by side on one buttoned black leather seat, the near window down on a run of dingy brick by-ways, a brass side-lamp burning on the frame, the fog-grey daylight coming in flat across their knees
cab.landmark: the brass side-lamp on the window frame
cab.landmark_size: is the height of a hand
cab.route: from the kerb outside Number 3 Lauriston Gardens, through the by-ways to Audley Court, and home again
cab.geometry: The two men sit side by side across the CENTRE of frame with Watson in the LEFT half and Holmes in the RIGHT. The open near window holds the whole LEFT edge with the passing brick fronts beyond it, and the brass side-lamp stands on its frame at the TOP LEFT at the height of a hand. The buttoned leather seat back runs across the frame behind their shoulders and the floor boards hold the BOTTOM edge

audley_court.described: Audley Court on a March afternoon: a flagged quadrangle walled in by sordid brick dwellings four storeys high, lines of grey washing strung from window to window across the air above, a scummed water pump standing at the CENTRE of the flags, and the narrow covered passage that lets into it holding the LEFT edge
audley_court.landmark: the green door of Number 46 at the quadrangle's far side
audley_court.landmark_size: is the height of a hand
audley_court.route: from the mouth of the covered passage, across the flags past the pump, to the green door of Number 46
audley_court.geometry: The covered passage holds the LEFT edge of frame and the green door of Number 46 stands at the CENTRE of the far side, growing from the height of a thumbnail to the height of a hand along the route. The scummed pump stands on the flags in the MIDDLE DISTANCE at the CENTRE, the brick dwellings rise across the whole TOP of frame, and the lines of washing cross the air above at the height of a second storey
audley_court.crowd: seven or eight ragged children squatting on the flags over a game of knucklebones, and two women in shawls filling cans at the pump

rance_parlour.described: The front parlour of Number 46 Audley Court: a low room with a horsehair sofa against the near wall, a small coal fire in a black grate, a deal table with a checked cloth, one sash window giving on the flagged court, and a framed print of a steamship hanging over the mantel
rance_parlour.landmark: the framed print of a steamship over the mantel
rance_parlour.landmark_size: is the height of a hand
rance_parlour.route: from the parlour door at the near wall to the horsehair sofa under the window
rance_parlour.geometry: The sash window holds the RIGHT edge of frame with the grey light of the court coming through it, the horsehair sofa stands under it along the RIGHT half, and the black grate with its coal fire holds the LEFT edge. The deal table with its checked cloth stands in the CENTRE at the height of a man's hip, and the framed steamship print hangs over the mantel at the TOP LEFT at the height of a hand

lauriston_gate.described: The garden gate of Number 3 Lauriston Gardens at two in the morning: a three-foot brick wall with wooden rails along its top, a wooden gate standing open on the yellow clay path, the shabby house front rising black behind it with one first-floor window lit yellow, and a street lamp burning through the fog at the kerb
lauriston_gate.landmark: the one lit first-floor window of Number 3
lauriston_gate.landmark_size: is the height of a thumbnail
lauriston_gate.route: from the kerb outside the brick wall, through the open gate, up the clay path toward the front door
lauriston_gate.geometry: The three-foot brick wall and its wooden rails cross the BOTTOM of frame nearest the camera with the open gate at the CENTRE, the yellow clay path runs up the CENTRE beyond it, and the black house front rises across the whole TOP of frame with its one lit first-floor window standing at the height of a thumbnail. The street lamp burns at the LEFT edge at the height of a hand, its light lying in a pool on the wet flags below

shots.frame: Medium inside the growler from its near side: the two men side by side on the buttoned leather seat, Watson in the LEFT half bare-headed and sunburnt, Holmes in the RIGHT half bare-headed, the bottle-green velvet at his open coat, the open window and the passing brick fronts beyond them at the LEFT edge.
shots.motion: The brick fronts travel past the open window at the horse's trot; Holmes turns his face from the window to Watson; his hands stay folded on the head of his stick.
shots.camera: on the near seat inside the growler, level with the two men's eyes and a long stride from them, a 35mm lens turned square across the seat. The flat fog-grey daylight comes in from the LEFT
shots.at_rest: Watson and Holmes sit side by side on the buttoned black leather seat, Watson in the LEFT half bare-headed and sunburnt, Holmes in the RIGHT half bare-headed, the bottle-green velvet at his open coat, the open near window holding the LEFT edge with a run of dingy brick fronts beyond it, the brass side-lamp burning at the TOP LEFT at the height of a hand, the buttoned seat back running across the frame behind their shoulders, and the floor boards holding the BOTTOM edge
shots.why: Holmes states the terms: evidence first, and his mind already made up.

shots.frame: Medium close on Holmes on the growler's near seat, bare-headed, the bottle-green velvet at his open coat, his head a quarter of the frame's height in the RIGHT half, the open window and the travelling brick fronts behind his shoulder at the LEFT.
shots.motion: Holmes lifts one hand off the head of his stick and counts two fingers into the air as he speaks the line; the hand comes back to the stick; his eyes go to the window.
shots.camera: on the near seat beside Watson, level with Holmes's eyes and a forearm from him, a 85mm lens turned on his face. The daylight from the open window falls across him from the LEFT
shots.at_rest: Holmes sits back on the buttoned leather seat, bare-headed, the bottle-green velvet at his open coat, his head a quarter of the frame's height in the RIGHT half, both hands on the head of his stick, the open window and the dingy brick fronts standing behind his shoulder at the LEFT edge, and the brass side-lamp burning at the TOP LEFT at the height of a hand
shots.why: The deduction has to be heard as arithmetic, not as magic.

shots.frame: Insert on Holmes's raised hand between the two men, two fingers standing up off the head of the black stick, the open window and the travelling brick fronts out of focus beyond.
shots.motion: The second finger comes up beside the first and the camera pushes straight in on the hand; the fingers hold; the brick fronts travel past behind them.
shots.camera: on the near seat beside Watson, level with the raised hand and a forearm from it, a 85mm lens turned on the fingers. The daylight from the open window falls across them from the LEFT
shots.at_rest: A bare hand stands at the CENTRE of frame off the silver head of a black walking stick with two fingers raised, a small white sticking plaster wound round the middle joint of the forefinger, the buttoned black leather of the seat filling the frame behind it, and the open window with the dingy brick fronts travelling beyond it out of focus at the LEFT edge
shots.why: The deduction is arithmetic, and a hand counting says so without a word.

shots.frame: Medium close past Holmes's shoulder onto Watson on the growler's near seat, bare-headed and sunburnt, his head a quarter of the frame's height in the RIGHT half, Holmes's dark shoulder standing out of focus across the whole LEFT edge.
shots.motion: Watson turns his head from the window to Holmes as he speaks the line; his brows draw together; his hand closes on the silver ball knob of the black walking stick.
shots.camera: on the near seat just behind Holmes's shoulder, level with Watson's eyes and a forearm from him, a 85mm lens turned past the shoulder onto his face. The daylight from the open window falls across him from behind the camera
shots.at_rest: Watson sits forward on the buttoned leather seat in the RIGHT half of frame, bare-headed and sunburnt, his head a quarter of the frame's height, his right hand closed on the silver ball knob of the black walking stick set upright between his boots, Holmes's dark shoulder and the back of his head standing out of focus across the whole LEFT edge, and the buttoned seat back running behind them
shots.why: Watson pushes back, so the method is tested and not admired.

shots.frame: Insert through the growler's open window: a wet grey by-way travelling past at the horse's trot, standing water lying in the ruts of the roadway and a blank brick flank beyond.
shots.motion: The wet roadway travels past the open window at the horse's trot and the standing water in the ruts catches the grey light; the camera holds a static shot.
shots.camera: on the near seat inside the growler, level with the open window and a forearm from it, a 50mm lens turned square out at the passing street. The flat grey daylight comes in from beyond
shots.at_rest: The open window of the growler frames a wet grey by-way, the standing water of a puddle lying across the ruts of the roadway at the CENTRE catching the flat light, a blank brick flank rising beyond it across the TOP of frame, and the dark edge of the window frame holding the LEFT and RIGHT edges
shots.why: The puddle he measured the man's age by, seen once.

shots.frame: Wide of Audley Court from the mouth of the covered passage: the flagged quadrangle walled in by brick dwellings four storeys high, lines of grey washing crossing the air above, the scummed pump at the CENTRE of the flags and the green door of Number 46 at the far side.
shots.motion: The lines of washing lift and fall together in the draught down the court and the camera pushes a hand's breadth in along the flags toward the green door.
shots.camera: in the mouth of the covered passage, level with a standing man's eyes and a long stride inside it, a 35mm lens turned across the quadrangle. The flat grey daylight falls from above
shots.at_rest: The flagged quadrangle of Audley Court stands walled in by sordid brick dwellings four storeys high, the lines of grey washing crossing the air above at the height of a second storey, the scummed water pump standing on the flags at the CENTRE in the MIDDLE DISTANCE, the green door of Number 46 at the CENTRE of the far side at the height of a thumbnail, and the covered passage holding the LEFT edge of frame
shots.crowd: seven or eight ragged children squatting on the flags over a game of knucklebones
shots.why: The squalor is the price of the evidence; it has to be seen once, whole.

shots.frame: Medium looking up between the brick dwellings of Audley Court: lines of grey washing crossing the air one above another, four storeys of sooted window openings rising either side, and a narrow strip of white sky closing the TOP of frame.
shots.motion: The lines of washing lift and fall together in the draught down the court and the camera tilts down a hand's breadth toward the flags; the children stay at their game.
shots.camera: on the flags at the mouth of the covered passage, level with a standing man's chest and a long stride inside it, a 50mm lens turned up the face of the dwellings. The flat grey daylight falls from above
shots.at_rest: Lines of grey washing cross the air one above another at the CENTRE of frame, the sooted brick dwellings rising four storeys either side with their window openings in rows, a narrow strip of white sky standing across the TOP of frame, and the flagged ground showing only along the BOTTOM edge far below
shots.why: The squalor is the price of the evidence; one picture pays it.

shots.frame: Medium on the two men crossing the flags at the CENTRE of the quadrangle, Watson in the LEFT half bare-headed and sunburnt, Holmes in the RIGHT half bare-headed, the bottle-green velvet at his open coat, the scummed pump behind them and the green door of Number 46 standing at the CENTRE of the far side.
shots.motion: The camera tracks beside them at a walking pace as Holmes steps out across the flags and Watson comes after him with the limp in his left leg; Holmes's eyes go to the green door.
shots.camera: on the flags beside the two men, level with their eyes and a long stride from them, a 35mm lens turned along the line of the walk. The flat grey daylight falls from above
shots.at_rest: Watson and Holmes stand on the flags at the CENTRE of the quadrangle, Watson in the LEFT half bare-headed and sunburnt, Holmes in the RIGHT half bare-headed, the bottle-green velvet at his open coat, the scummed water pump standing behind them at the CENTRE, the green door of Number 46 at the far side at the height of a finger, the brick dwellings rising across the whole TOP of frame and the lines of washing crossing the air above them
shots.crowd: two women in shawls filling cans at the pump, and three ragged children watching from the flags
shots.why: Walking the ground keeps the geography real before the room closes in.

shots.frame: Medium of the low parlour from the door: Rance standing in the CENTRE, his navy jacket open at the throat, Holmes in the RIGHT half bare-headed, the bottle-green velvet at his open coat and Watson at the LEFT edge bare-headed and sunburnt, the coal fire in its black grate at the LEFT and the sash window giving on the court at the RIGHT.
shots.motion: Rance pushes the parlour door to behind them and rubs one hand over his sandy side-whiskers; his eyes travel from Holmes to Watson; his shoulders come down.
shots.camera: just inside the parlour door, level with the three men's eyes and a long stride from them, a 35mm lens turned into the room. The grey light of the court comes through the sash window at the RIGHT
shots.at_rest: Rance stands in the CENTRE of the low parlour, his navy jacket open at the throat, Holmes in the RIGHT half bare-headed, the bottle-green velvet at his open coat and Watson at the LEFT edge bare-headed and sunburnt. The black grate with its small coal fire holds the LEFT edge, the deal table with its checked cloth stands in the CENTRE at the height of a man's hip, the horsehair sofa stands under the sash window along the RIGHT, and the framed steamship print hangs over the mantel at the TOP LEFT
shots.why: Establish the three of them in one frame before the room becomes faces.

shots.frame: Medium close on Holmes in the parlour, bare-headed, the bottle-green velvet at his open coat, his head a quarter of the frame's height in the RIGHT half, the sash window and the grey court beyond it at the RIGHT edge.
shots.motion: Holmes turns a half-sovereign over in his fingers as he speaks the line and holds it up between finger and thumb; his eyes stay on Rance; the coin catches the firelight.
shots.camera: on the parlour boards beside the deal table, level with Holmes's eyes and a forearm from him, a 85mm lens turned on his face. The firelight falls across him from the LEFT
shots.at_rest: Holmes stands at the deal table in the low parlour, bare-headed, the bottle-green velvet at his open coat, his head a quarter of the frame's height in the RIGHT half, a half-sovereign held up between his finger and thumb at the height of his chest, the sash window and the grey court standing at the RIGHT edge, and the checked cloth of the table running across the BOTTOM of frame
shots.why: The coin buys the story; the chapter says so plainly and so does the shot.

shots.frame: Insert on the half-sovereign turning between Holmes's finger and thumb above the checked cloth of the deal table, the coin catching the firelight.
shots.motion: The half-sovereign turns over once between the finger and thumb and the camera pushes straight in on it; the gold catches the firelight and holds.
shots.camera: at the deal table, level with the turning coin and a hand's breadth from it, a 100mm lens turned on the gold. The firelight falls across it from the LEFT
shots.at_rest: A half-sovereign stands on edge between a bare finger and thumb at the CENTRE of frame, its gold catching the firelight, a small white sticking plaster wound round the middle joint of the forefinger, the checked cloth of the deal table lying below and behind out of focus, and the dark of the low parlour closing the edges
shots.why: The coin is what buys the story; the chapter says so and so does the shot.

shots.frame: Close on Rance seated on the horsehair sofa, his navy jacket open at the throat, his head a third of the frame's height, the sash window and the grey light of the court behind his shoulder.
shots.motion: Rance knits his brows and sets both hands flat on his knees as he speaks the line; his chin comes up; his eyes go to the coin in Holmes's hand.
shots.camera: on the parlour boards in front of the horsehair sofa, level with Rance's eyes and a forearm from him, a 85mm lens turned on his face. The grey window light falls across him from the RIGHT
shots.at_rest: Rance sits well back on the horsehair sofa, his navy jacket open at the throat, his head a third of the frame's height, both hands flat on his knees, the sash window and the grey light of the flagged court standing behind his shoulder at the RIGHT, and the arm of the sofa running across the BOTTOM of frame
shots.why: His face has to be learned now, so the turn later lands on someone known.

shots.frame: Insert on Rance's two broad hands set flat on his knees on the horsehair sofa, the dark serge of his trousers below them and the sofa's scrolled arm at the RIGHT.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in on the hands across the whole shot, travelling a forearm from the knees to the fingers, and the right hand closes into a loose fist as it comes.
shots.camera: on the parlour boards in front of the horsehair sofa, level with the seated man's knees and a forearm from them, a 85mm lens turned down on the hands. The grey window light falls across them from the RIGHT
shots.at_rest: Two broad weathered hands lie flat on a pair of knees at the CENTRE of frame, the dark serge of the trousers filling the frame below them, the horsehair of the sofa standing behind, and the scrolled wooden arm of the sofa holding the RIGHT edge
shots.why: A man settling to tell a long story does it with his hands.

shots.frame: Wide of the garden gate of Number 3 at two in the morning: the three-foot brick wall and its wooden rails crossing the BOTTOM of frame, the open wooden gate at the CENTRE, the black house front rising behind with one first-floor window lit yellow, and the street lamp burning through the fog at the LEFT.
shots.motion: The fog rolls a hand's breadth across the pool of lamplight on the wet flags and the camera pushes in a hand's breadth toward the open gate; the lit window holds its yellow.
shots.camera: on the wet flags of the pavement outside the brick wall, level with a standing man's eyes and a long stride from the gate, a 35mm lens turned up the clay path. The street lamp burns from the LEFT
shots.at_rest: The three-foot brick wall and its wooden rails cross the BOTTOM of frame with the wooden gate standing open at the CENTRE, the yellow clay path running up the CENTRE beyond it, the shabby house front rising black across the whole TOP of frame with one first-floor window lit yellow at the height of a thumbnail, the street lamp burning at the LEFT edge at the height of a hand, and its light lying in a pool on the wet flags below
shots.why: Rance's memory has to be a place, not a description of a place.

shots.frame: Insert on the one lit first-floor window of Number 3, its yellow candlelight standing behind the blank glass, the fog lying grey across the pane and the black brickwork wet around it.
shots.motion: The candle flame behind the glass leans and steadies and the camera pushes straight in on the lit pane; the fog thickens across it by a hand's breadth.
shots.camera: on the wet flags below the house front, level with the lit window and a long stride back from it, a 85mm lens turned up at the pane. The street lamp burns from the LEFT
shots.at_rest: One first-floor window of Number 3 fills the frame, its black-painted sash weathered and its brickwork wet, the yellow light of a single candle standing behind the blank glass, the fog lying grey across the pane, and the dark of the empty rooms either side holding the edges
shots.why: One lit window in an empty house is the whole reason he went in.

shots.frame: Medium close past Holmes's shoulder onto Rance on the horsehair sofa, his navy jacket open at the throat, his head a quarter of the frame's height in the RIGHT half, Holmes's dark shoulder standing out of focus across the whole LEFT edge.
shots.motion: Rance lifts one hand off his knee and turns it over as he speaks the line and the camera pulls back a hand's breadth; the hand comes down; his eyes go past the shoulder to the fire.
shots.camera: on the parlour boards just behind Holmes's shoulder, level with Rance's eyes and a forearm from him, a 85mm lens turned past the shoulder onto his face. The grey window light falls across him from the RIGHT
shots.at_rest: Rance sits forward on the horsehair sofa in the RIGHT half of frame, his navy jacket open at the throat, his head a quarter of the frame's height, one hand lifted off his knee at the height of his chest, Holmes's dark shoulder standing out of focus across the whole LEFT edge, and the sash window with the grey light of the flagged court filling the wall behind him
shots.why: He is proud of the story and does not know which part matters.

shots.frame: Close on Holmes's face over the deal table, bare-headed, the bottle-green velvet at his open coat, his head a third of the frame's height, the coal fire burning small and red at the LEFT edge behind him.
shots.motion: Holmes comes down over the checked cloth until his face fills the frame as he speaks the line; his head tips; his eyes hold steady on Rance.
shots.camera: at the deal table, level with Holmes's eyes and a hand's breadth closer than a forearm, a 100mm lens turned up at his face. The firelight falls across him from the LEFT
shots.at_rest: Holmes's face fills the CENTRE of frame come down over the deal table, bare-headed, the bottle-green velvet at his open coat, his head a third of the frame's height, the checked cloth running across the BOTTOM edge below him, the coal fire burning small and red at the LEFT edge, and the low papered wall of the parlour standing dark behind his shoulder
shots.why: THE TURN: Holmes asks the one question nobody else thought to ask.

shots.frame: Medium on the open garden gate from the pavement: a tall man in a brown overcoat leaning back against the wooden rails with his face muffled to the eyes in a dark comforter, the street lamp burning at the LEFT and the black house front behind him.
shots.motion: The tall man's shoulders roll against the rails as he sings and one arm comes up over the wood; the fog travels across the lamplight; his muffled face stays turned down.
shots.camera: on the wet flags of the pavement a long stride from the rails, level with the tall man's chest, a 50mm lens turned along the wall. The street lamp burns from the LEFT behind him
shots.at_rest: A tall man in a brown overcoat leans back against the wooden rails beside the open gate, the lower part of his face muffled to the eyes in a dark comforter and his hat brim down over his brow, one arm hooked over the wood and his boots planted wide on the wet flags. The street lamp burns at the LEFT edge with the fog travelling through its light, and the black house front rises behind him across the TOP of frame
shots.why: The murderer, seen at last, and drawn so his face stays the next chapter's.

shots.frame: Insert on the tall man's bare hand hooked over the wooden rail, the knuckles raw and red in the lamplight, the wet wood dark under it and the fog beyond.
shots.motion: The bare hand tightens on the wooden rail and slides a thumb's width along the wet wood, and the camera pushes straight in on the raw knuckles.
shots.camera: on the wet flags at the wooden rails, level with the hooked hand and a forearm from it, a 85mm lens turned along the rail. The street lamp burns from the LEFT
shots.at_rest: A bare sunburnt hand is hooked over the top of the wooden rail at the CENTRE of frame, its knuckles raw and red in the lamplight, the wet dark wood running across the frame under it, the black brick of the garden wall below, and the fog standing grey beyond the rail
shots.why: The nails were long: Holmes said so in the cab, and here is the hand.

shots.frame: Close on Rance from the side, his navy jacket open at the throat, his head a third of the frame's height in the LEFT half, the framed steamship print hanging on the wall behind his shoulder at the RIGHT.
shots.motion: Rance turns his face to the camera and grins as he speaks the line and the camera pushes in a hand's breadth; the grin stays; his shoulders come up and settle.
shots.camera: on the parlour boards at the end of the horsehair sofa, level with Rance's eyes and a forearm from him, a 85mm lens turned along the sofa at his cheek. The firelight falls across him from the LEFT
shots.at_rest: Rance's grinning face stands in the LEFT half of frame turned three-quarters to the camera, his navy jacket open at the throat, his head a third of the frame's height, the framed steamship print hanging on the papered wall behind his shoulder at the RIGHT, and the horsehair of the sofa back running dark across the BOTTOM of frame
shots.why: He tells the worst mistake of his life as an amusing anecdote.

shots.frame: Medium on Holmes standing away from the deal table toward the sash window, bare-headed, the bottle-green velvet at his open coat, his head a quarter of the frame's height in the RIGHT half, the whole checked table and the black grate standing across the frame below him.
shots.motion: Holmes straightens off the table and turns his face to the sash window as he speaks the line; his hand closes at his side; his chin lifts.
shots.camera: against the parlour's near wall, level with Holmes's chest and two long strides from him, a 35mm lens turned across the room. The grey window light falls on him from the RIGHT
shots.at_rest: Holmes stands clear of the deal table turned toward the sash window, bare-headed, the bottle-green velvet at his open coat, his head a quarter of the frame's height in the RIGHT half, the deal table with its checked cloth standing across the CENTRE at the height of his hip, the black grate with its coal fire at the LEFT edge, and the grey light of the flagged court coming through the window at the RIGHT
shots.why: Holmes hears the description and knows the man walked away.

shots.frame: Full of the low parlour from the window side: Holmes at the parlour door in the LEFT half bare-headed, the bottle-green velvet at his open coat, Watson beyond him in the doorway bare-headed and sunburnt, and Rance still seated on the horsehair sofa at the BOTTOM RIGHT with his back three-quarters to the camera.
shots.motion: Holmes lays the half-sovereign down on the checked cloth and follows Watson out through the parlour door; the camera pushes in on Rance across the whole shot, travelling two long strides, as he turns his head after them.
shots.camera: at the sash window with its back to the court, level with a standing man's chest and three long strides from the door, a 35mm lens turned back across the room. The grey window light falls from behind the camera
shots.at_rest: Holmes stands at the open parlour door in the LEFT half of frame bare-headed, the bottle-green velvet at his open coat, Watson stands beyond him in the doorway bare-headed and sunburnt, and Rance sits on the horsehair sofa at the BOTTOM RIGHT with his back three-quarters to the camera his navy jacket open at the throat. The half-sovereign lies on the checked cloth of the deal table in the CENTRE, the black grate stands at the far wall, and the framed steamship print hangs over the mantel at the TOP CENTRE
shots.why: The coin is paid and the room is finished with; the picture says so.

shots.frame: Close on Watson's face turned to the open window of the growler, bare-headed and sunburnt, his head a third of the frame's height, the passing brick fronts travelling beyond him out of focus.
shots.motion: The light of the passing fronts crosses Watson's face in bars as he speaks the line and he turns his head in from the window; his eyes come round; his jaw sets.
shots.camera: on the near seat with its back to the horses, level with Watson's eyes and a forearm from him, a 100mm lens turned on his face past the window frame. The travelling daylight falls across him from the LEFT
shots.at_rest: Watson's face fills the LEFT half of frame turned three-quarters to the open window, bare-headed and sunburnt, his head a third of the frame's height, the window frame standing as a dark upright at the CENTRE and the dingy brick fronts travelling beyond it out of focus, and the buttoned leather of the seat back dark at the RIGHT edge
shots.why: Watson asks the audience's question so the button can answer it.

shots.frame: Close on Holmes leaning forward off the growler's seat back, bare-headed, the bottle-green velvet at his open coat, his head a third of the frame's height, the brass side-lamp burning behind his shoulder at the TOP LEFT.
shots.motion: Holmes comes forward until his face fills the frame and lifts one finger between himself and the camera as he speaks the line; the finger stays up; his eyes hold.
shots.camera: on the near seat beside Watson, level with Holmes's eyes and a hand's breadth closer than a forearm, a 100mm lens turned square on his face. The brass lamp burns behind his shoulder from the LEFT
shots.at_rest: Holmes's face fills the CENTRE of frame leaning forward off the buttoned seat back, bare-headed, the bottle-green velvet at his open coat, his head a third of the frame's height, one forefinger raised at the height of his chin, the brass side-lamp burning small and gold behind his shoulder at the TOP LEFT, and the dark of the growler's roof closing the edges
shots.why: THE BUTTON: the ring is the line he will fish with, and he says so.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: It was one o'clock when we left the empty house on Lauriston Gardens.

lines.speaker: sherlock_holmes
lines.text: There is nothing like first hand evidence. My mind is entirely made up.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: He had read a man's height off the length of his stride.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: And his age off the width of a puddle the fellow stepped across.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Surely, I said, you are not as certain as you pretend to be.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: We drove into the dingiest and dreariest of a long succession of by-ways.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Audley Court was not an attractive locality.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: We picked our way among dirty children and under lines of discoloured linen.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Constable John Rance was in bed, and came down looking irritable.

lines.speaker: sherlock_holmes
lines.text: We thought that we should like to hear it all from your own lips.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Holmes took a half-sovereign from his pocket and played with it.

lines.speaker: john_rance
lines.text: I shall be most happy to tell you anything I can.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: His beat ran from ten at night until six in the morning.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: At two o'clock he saw a light in the window of the empty house.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: There was a candle burning, and a dead man on the boards.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: He had walked the room, and knelt by the body, and tried the kitchen door.

lines.speaker: sherlock_holmes
lines.text: What sort of a man was he?

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: A drunken fellow had been leaning on the railings, singing at the top of his voice.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: A long chap, with a red face, the lower part muffled round.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: They had propped him up between them and let him walk away.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Holmes said nothing at all for a moment.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: He laid the half-sovereign down and we left our informant uncomfortable.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: The blundering fool, said Holmes, as we drove back to our lodgings.

lines.speaker: sherlock_holmes
lines.text: The ring, man, the ring. That was what he came back for.
